PG.rationale: PG is a high-quality, structurally durable consumer staples franchise with strong profitability (ROE 29.7%, net margin 18.6%), a fortress balance sheet, and a 70-year dividend growth streak. The business is growing revenue +7.4% YoY and EPS +5.8% YoY despite sequential QoQ softness (-4.4% revenue, -8.4% EPS). Valuation at PE 23.3x sits in the lower half of its 12-month range (21.7x-26.3x), suggesting the market has already priced in near-term cost headwinds. However, the confirmed $1B FY2027 oil headwind and $400M tariff impact represent real near-term earnings pressure that will likely produce a margin trough before restructuring savings and productivity gains materialize. The stock's 12.7% underperformance over 3 months reflects this overhang. The score is modestly positive — the franchise quality and valuation support are real, but the near-term cost headwinds are material and the growth algorithm (mid-single-digit organic sales, mid-to-high-single-digit EPS growth) is modest, limiting re-rating potential until the cost trajectory clarifies. The Q3 FY2026 earnings beat (04/24/2026) and 3% organic growth provide some near-term positive signal, but the cautious FY2026 guidance toward the lower EPS range tempers this.
key_factors: Q3 FY2026 revenue $21.23B, +7.4% YoY; EPS diluted $1.63, +5.8% YoY — strong annual growth despite QoQ softness (-4.4% revenue, -8.4% EPS)
ROE 29.7% and net margin 18.6% — high, stable profitability metrics unchanged across the window
Operating cash flow $4.04B exceeds net income $3.95B in Q3 — strong cash conversion; balance sheet equity $54.73B, D/E 1.35x
PE diluted 23.32x in lower half of 12-month range (21.7x-26.3x); P/B 6.916x near lower end of 6.4x-7.8x range — valuation not stretched vs own history
Confirmed $1B after-tax FY2027 oil cost headwind (Brent ~$100) and $400M tariff impact — dominant near-term earnings pressure
FY2026 guidance maintained organic sales growth 0-4% and core EPS $6.83-$7.09 but guided toward lower end due to commodity/tariff headwinds
Restructuring with up to 7,000 job cuts by FY2027 aimed at defending margins; productivity programs delivered 560bp savings in Q4 FY2025
Stock down 12.7% over 3 months, underperforming S&P 500; 18.7% below December 2024 record of $172.51
70 consecutive years of dividend increases; April 2026 raise to $1.0885/share; payout ratio ~63.6%
Q3 FY2026 earnings beat consensus (revenue +3.6%, EPS $1.59 adjusted vs $1.56 consensus); organic sales growth 3% beat by ~109bp
